rationale: Both new requirements sit on existing machinery. The audit requirement needs a record path that survives debug capture being off, and the shape of that record already exists: rejectQueuedInput already assembles reason, detailReason, barrierReason, queuedMs and generation values. The contract requirement needs no code at all, because it states behaviour the code already has.
conditions: The audit requirement must carry its own no-raw-content criterion. The constraint at line 41 of the SRS scopes raw-input suppression to backpressure and reconnect handling, so authority-fencing drops fall outside it.
The audit requirement must name inputSeqStart and inputSeqEnd rather than a single inputSeq. WsRouter.ts:4847-4856 rejects a lone inputSeq explicitly.
The contract requirement must state that the blocker does not gate promotion. promoteSession never reads retained.blockers.

corrected_premise.what_was_assumed: A session carrying mutation-identity-missing cannot be promoted to authority.
corrected_premise.what_the_code_shows: TerminalAuthorityProductionAdapter.promoteSession:2626-2664 gates on responder capability, checkpoint presence, prepareTerminalAuthorityPromotionCandidate and bootstrap replay supersession. None of those reads retained.blockers, and prepareTerminalAuthorityPromotionCandidate:2775-2814 inspects only transitionEpoch, limitedSessionSelected, admission.mode and serverRecoveryAcks.
corrected_premise.actual_effect: canary.eligible drops to false at SessionManager.ts:7565-7566 and the session appears in diagnosticBlockers at :2895. The only consumer of canary.eligible is test code.
corrected_premise.why_it_matters: Writing the assumed contract would have pinned a guarantee the runtime does not provide, and the next reader would have trusted it.
